report:
Feature 1 (accounts and notes) is written and committed on the current branch as `8c331b1`, not pushed. The gate (`yarn architecture gate --base 1cf72f4… --mode architecture`) passes on the committed tree, and the storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. That gate run includes all checks: conventions, format, lint, typecheck, 105 unit tests and 14 end-to-end tests. I didn't start a server on 18500; the end-to-end suites boot the application on a free port and call it over HTTP.

**Architecture task**
- I added two contexts, **Accounts** and **Notes**. Both are declared in `conventions/typescript.yaml` and described in `conventions/domain.yaml`, with subdomain, purpose and vocabulary.
- There is no relationship between them, as the storm's hot spot decided. Notes gets the owner from the caller's id and never asks Accounts anything.
- The decision is recorded in `docs/adr/0001-accounts-and-notes-contexts.md`.

**The feature**
- **Accounts:**
  - Signing up is a command; the outcome's `result` is the new account id.
  - Two rules are checked at sign-up: a password has at least 8 characters, and an email is used by one account only. The second is also enforced when saving, so two sign-ups racing for the same email can't both succeed.
  - Only a scrypt hash of the password is stored, and no response ever returns it.
  - `GET /accounts/me` answers 403 to an anonymous caller.
  - The bearer-token check is passed to the server's `authenticate` hook. A missing, forged or expired token just makes the request anonymous.
- **Notes:**
  - Title is required and at most 100 characters; the text may be empty.
  - Edit, archive and restore work as specified, and an archived note can't be edited until it is restored.
  - The list is most recent first, and `createdAt` is an ISO 8601 string.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Login:** the storm says it records nothing and names no command for it, so I made it neither a command nor a query. It is a small service (`LogIn`) that the login route calls directly, answering 200 `{ token }` or 401. Wrong email and wrong password give the same 401 body.
- **Hashing and tokens:** the binding allows `jose` and `bcryptjs`, but neither is installed, so I used Node's built-in `crypto` (scrypt hashing, HMAC-signed tokens). Tokens are signed with `TOKEN_SECRET`; without it, a random secret is generated at startup, so tokens don't survive a restart (neither do the in-memory accounts).
- **Anonymous callers on Notes:** the table gives 403 only for `POST /notes` and `GET`. Since "an anonymous caller can do none of it", I also answer 403 on edit, archive and restore, before anything is accepted.
- **Someone else's note:** acting on it gives an `ERROR` outcome of type `NoteNotFound`, the same as an unknown id. Reading it gives 404, as the table says.
- **Missing fields:** the request schemas don't require `title`, `email` or `password`. A missing one becomes an `ERROR` outcome rather than a 400, because the brief says a refusal is an `ERROR` outcome.
- **Every account is an ordinary user.** There is no administrator yet.
- **Concepts list:** I added the files that now show each concept to the `concepts` section of `typescript.yaml`, as its header asks. That regenerated part of `README.md`. It's an edit to `conventions` beyond declaring the contexts; architecture mode allows it.

Feature 2 (pin a note) is done and committed on the current branch as `810da58`, not pushed. The gate (`--base a284a6e… --mode architecture`) passes, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. No server was started.

There was no architecture task: it's a feature inside the existing Notes context, with no new context, relationship or ADR.

**What it does**
- **Pin and unpin:**
  - The owner pins a note with `POST /notes/{id}/pin` and unpins it with `POST /notes/{id}/unpin`; both answer 202.
  - Pinning a note that's already pinned, or unpinning one that isn't, gives an `ERROR` outcome.
- **Archived notes:**
  - An archived note can't be pinned.
  - Archiving doesn't remove the pin, and an archived note can still be unpinned. This follows the storm's hot spot.
- **Reading notes:**
  - `GET /notes` and `GET /notes/{id}` now include `pinned: boolean`.
  - The list puts pinned notes first, and within each group the most recent first.
- **Events:** pinning records `NotePinned` and unpinning records `NoteUnpinned`. Nothing reacts to them yet, as the storm decided.
- **Someone else's note:** pinning or unpinning it gives the same "not found" refusal as the other note commands. An anonymous caller gets 403 on both routes.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Order inside the pinned group:** I used the date the note was written, not the time it was pinned, because the brief says "within each group, most recent first" and a note's `createdAt` is the date it already shows.
- **Archived pinned notes in the list:** the list already includes archived notes, so an archived note that is still pinned stays in the pinned group, at the top.
- **Which check comes first:** pinning an archived note that's already pinned is refused as "archived" rather than "already pinned". Either answer is a refusal; I picked the archive check first.

Feature 3 (tags on a note) is done and committed on the current branch as `7b7d99e`, not pushed. The gate (`--base f1b5400… --mode architecture`) passes, including the unit and end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. No server was started.

As with pinning, there was no architecture task: tags live inside the Notes context, with no new context, relationship or ADR.

**What it does**
- **Adding a tag:** `POST /notes/{id}/tags` with `{ tag }` answers 202.
  - A tag must be one lowercase word: letters a–z, digits and hyphens, 1 to 30 characters.
  - Anything else gives an `ERROR` outcome, as typed. `Work`, ` work`, `two words` and `café` are refused, not rewritten.
- **Removing a tag:** `DELETE /notes/{id}/tags/{tag}` answers 202.
- **Other refusals:** adding a tag the note already has, removing one it doesn't have, an eleventh tag, and adding or removing tags on an archived note (until it is restored).
- **Reading:** each note now shows `tags`, in the order they were added. `GET /notes?tag=work` returns the caller's notes that carry that tag, in the same order as the full list (pinned first, then most recent).
- **Events:** each change records `NoteTagged` or `NoteUntagged`. Nothing reacts to them yet, as the storm says.
- **Other callers:** someone else's note answers "not found" here as everywhere else, and anonymous callers get 403 on all the new routes.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Which refusal wins:** when several rules fail at once, a note that isn't yours is checked first, then archived, then a malformed tag, then duplicate or missing tag, then the limit of 10. They're all refusals, so it only changes which reason the outcome gives.
- **Removing a malformed tag:** `DELETE` with something that isn't a valid tag (`/tags/Work`) is refused as an invalid tag rather than "this note doesn't have it". Either way it's an `ERROR`.
- **Filtering by a bad tag:** `GET /notes?tag=` with an empty or malformed value returns an empty list, not an error. No note can carry such a tag, and the storm says the filter is a filter on the list, not a new list.
- **The filter includes archived notes**, like the unfiltered list does.
- **Removing then re-adding a tag** puts it at the end of the order.
- **A `DELETE` sent with `Content-Type: application/json` and an empty body** is rejected by the web server with 400 before reaching the application. Clients should send no body on that route.

Feature 4 (share a note) is done and committed on the current branch as `55ed985`, not pushed. The gate (`--base 1a44c5e… --mode architecture`) passes, including 131 unit tests and 23 end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. No server was started.

**Architecture task**
Refusing to share with an account that doesn't exist needs a new relationship, Accounts → Notes. I declared it and recorded it:
- **Domain map:** `conventions/domain.yaml` now declares Accounts → Notes. Notes asks a yes/no question through a port it owns, and Accounts serves it.
- **The port and the rule:** Notes owns the port `IAccountDirectory`, which answers whether an account id exists. The new `NoteSharing` domain service holds the rule that a note is shared only with an existing account.
- **The adapter:** `AccountsAccountDirectory`, in Notes' infrastructure, answers the port from Accounts' read model. It is the only Notes file that imports Accounts. Accounts' wiring now exports that read model (`accountQueries`).
- **The record:** `docs/adr/0002-notes-asks-accounts-through-an-owned-port.md`. It also explains why I chose a port over an event: the question is one yes/no, asked only when sharing, so Notes shouldn't keep its own copy of every account. ADR 1, which said the contexts had no relationship, now points to it.

**What it does**
- **Sharing:** `POST /notes/{id}/share` with `{ accountId }` answers 202. It gives an `ERROR` outcome when:
  - the account doesn't exist;
  - the note is already shared with that account;
  - the account is the owner's own;
  - the note is archived.
- **What a recipient can do:** read the note with `GET /notes/{id}` (200), and see the notes shared with them at `GET /notes/shared`, most recent first, each with `ownerId`.
- **What a recipient can't do:** edit, archive, restore, pin, tag or share the note. Each of those gives an `ERROR` outcome saying only the owner can change it. Anyone else still gets "not found".
- **What the owner sees:** every note now carries `ownerId`. The owner's `GET /notes/{id}` also shows `sharedWith`, the account ids in the order the note was shared with them.
- **Event:** sharing records `NoteShared`. Nothing reacts to it yet.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **The recipient's refusal says why.** The note exists for them, so I didn't reuse the owner-only "not found" refusal.
- **Order of checks:** the account's existence is checked before the note's own rules. So sharing someone else's note with an account that doesn't exist is refused as "no such account" rather than "not found". Both are refusals.
- **Same fields for everyone:** a recipient sees the same fields as the owner except `sharedWith`, including the owner's `pinned` and `tags`. Hiding them wasn't asked for.
- **The shared list ignores pins,** which order only the owner's own list. It includes archived notes, shown with `archived: true`.
- **Shared notes are not in the recipient's own `GET /notes`,** which stays "my notes".
- **There is no way to un-share yet.** If an account ever disappeared it would stay in `sharedWith`; accounts can't be closed today. ADR 2 notes this.

Feature 5 (notify recipients when a shared note is archived) is done and committed on the current branch as `80335aa`, not pushed. The gate (`--base 562a191… --mode architecture`) passes on the committed tree, including 139 unit tests and 26 end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. No server was started.

**Architecture task**
This needed a new context and a new relationship. Both are declared and recorded in `docs/adr/0003-notifications-context-hears-notes-archived.md`.
- **New context, Notifications** (a supporting subdomain): declared in `conventions/typescript.yaml`, described in `conventions/domain.yaml`, and registered in the composition root under `/notifications`.
  - Its aggregate is `Notification`: one recipient, a `kind` (`note-archived` today), the note's id and title, and when it happened.
  - It records `NotificationCreated`.
- **New relationship, Notes → Notifications, carried by an event:**
  - `NoteArchivedEvent` now carries the title, the owner, the accounts the note was shared with at that moment, and when.
  - A Notes handler publishes it as `NoteArchivedIntegrationEvent`, the contract in `src/SharedKernel/Application/IntegrationEvents/NoteIntegrationEvents.ts`. It goes through the outbox on every archiving.
  - In Notifications, a handler translates that event into one notification per recipient, never the owner. It saves them in one transaction, so a failure undoes all of them.
  - Notifications never asks Notes anything, and Notes never imports Notifications.

**What it does**
- Each time the owner archives a note, every account it is shared with at that moment gets a notification. The owner gets none, and a note shared with nobody notifies nobody.
- Archiving, restoring and archiving again gives one notification per archiving.
- `GET /notifications` lists the caller's own notifications, most recent first, with exactly `{ id, kind: 'note-archived', noteId, noteTitle, archivedAt }`. An anonymous caller gets 403, and nobody can see anyone else's.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Notifications arrive a moment after the archive's outcome.** They're created by a reaction to the event, so a client reading the archive's outcome as `SUCCESS` may list its notifications a few milliseconds before they exist. The end-to-end suite waits for them.
- **The title is the one the note had when archived.** Editing the note afterwards doesn't change notifications already sent.
- **Notes publishes the fact on every archiving, even when the note is shared with nobody.** Notifications then simply creates none. I preferred that to Notes deciding who should hear of it.
- **Feature 7's reminders aren't built yet.** The list is a union of shapes told apart by `kind`, so reminders can join it. The single factory, `Notification.noteArchived`, and the stored fields (`noteId`, `noteTitle`, `occurredAt`) may need widening when they arrive.

Feature 6 (a plan and a ten-note quota) is done and committed on the current branch as `24ab350`, not pushed. The gate (`--base 24dc413… --mode architecture`) passes on the committed tree, including 154 unit tests and 30 end-to-end tests. The storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. No server was started.

**Architecture task**
The storm put plans in a context of their own, which Notes asks through a port it owns. That's a new context and a new relationship, recorded in `docs/adr/0004-plans-context-and-the-note-quota.md`.
- **New context, Plans:** declared in the binding, described in the domain map, and served under `/plans`.
  - Its aggregate is `Plan`, one per account. An account that never chose a plan has none stored and is on Free.
  - A value object holds the two plans and their limits: Free keeps 10 notes, Unlimited has no limit.
- **New relationship, Plans → Notes**, the same shape as the account directory in ADR 2:
  - Notes owns the port `IPlanLimits`, which answers "how many notes may this account keep".
  - The quota rule lives in a new `NoteWriting` domain service. It asks the limit, counts every note the person owns (archived ones included), and refuses one more. Writing a note now goes through it.
  - `PlansPlanLimits`, in Notes' infrastructure, answers the port from Plans' read model. It is the only Notes file that imports Plans, and Plans knows nothing of notes.

**What it does**
- `GET /plans/me` answers `{ plan: 'free', noteLimit: 10 }` or `{ plan: 'unlimited', noteLimit: null }`, and 403 to an anonymous caller.
- `PUT /plans/me` with `{ plan }` answers 202 and records `PlanChanged`. Any value other than `'free'` or `'unlimited'`, including a missing one, gives an `ERROR` outcome.
- On Free, an eleventh note gives an `ERROR` outcome of type `NoteQuotaReached`, with archived notes counting toward the ten.
- Back on Free with more than ten notes, the person keeps them all; only writing a new one is refused.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Switching to the plan you're already on succeeds and changes nothing.** Nothing is recorded. Unlike pinning twice, which the earlier storm said to refuse, nothing says to refuse this, and a `PUT` is naturally repeatable.
- **Which refusal wins:** a blank or too-long title is reported before the quota.
- **The quota isn't safe against two simultaneous writes.** Two notes written at the very same moment by someone at nine could both get through, because counting and saving aren't one locked step. ADR 4 says what a real database would need.
- **Test change:** the Notes end-to-end suite's main account writes more than ten notes, so its setup now switches that account to Unlimited. The quota itself is tested in the new Plans suite.

Feature 7 (remind a note at a time) is done and committed on the current branch as `2310323`, not pushed. The gate (`--base 026f1d4… --mode architecture`) passes, including 164 unit tests and 34 end-to-end tests. I ran the end-to-end suite twice more because the reminder tests depend on timing; both runs passed. The storm owes nothing, so it is now `done: true`. No server was started.

**No architecture task.** The storm adds two facts, `ReminderScheduled` and `ReminderCancelled`, to the existing Notes → Notifications relationship, so there's no new context or relationship and no new ADR. I updated the domain map's vocabulary and added a short note to ADR 3 explaining the extension.

**What it does**
- **Scheduling:** `POST /notes/{id}/reminders` with `{ remindAt }` answers 202. One reminder per note, owner only.
  - Refused: a moment that is now or in the past, an archived note, and a moment that isn't ISO 8601 with a time zone.
  - Scheduling again replaces the reminder; archiving the note drops it.
  - `GET /notes/{id}` shows `remindAt`, or `null`.
- **Facts Notes publishes:** replacing or archiving a reminder whose moment hasn't come records `ReminderCancelled`. Scheduling records `ReminderScheduled`, with the note's title at that moment.
- **Telling the owner:** Notifications plans a `reminder` notification for the owner only; the accounts the note is shared with get nothing.
  - It appears in `GET /notifications` once its moment has passed, with exactly `{ id, kind: 'reminder', noteId, noteTitle, remindAt }`.
  - Nothing watches the clock: the list decides what's due when it is read, as the storm said.
- **Cancelling:** a cancelled reminder is never shown. One whose moment had already come before the archiving stays in the list.
- **Order:** the list is most recent first, archivings by when they happened and reminders by their moment.

**What was unclear, and what I decided**
- **Each reminder has its own id.** Notes publishes "old reminder cancelled" and "new reminder scheduled" from two separate reactions, which can reach Notifications in either order. The id lets a cancellation remove exactly the reminder it names and never the replacement.
- **A cancellation arriving before its own scheduling is ignored.** If that ever happened, the reminder would later be shown anyway. I judged it unlikely, since the two come from different requests, and didn't build for it.
- **The moment must carry a time zone** (`Z` or an offset), so `2026-10-31T09:00:00` alone is refused. Otherwise its meaning would depend on the server's time zone.
- **A reminder whose moment has passed still shows on the note** until it's replaced or the note is archived. "Its reminder's moment, or none" didn't say whether a past one should disappear.
- **Restoring a note doesn't bring its reminder back.**

**Tidy-up:** feature 6 had left the "Unknown, or someone else's" doc comment above the quota exception, so this commit moves it back onto `NoteNotFoundException`.
